newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end slightly higher.

text.p: Jan 3 - U.S. debt futures ended slightly higher in light trade. Both bonds and Euros trimmed gains due, in part, to a BusinessWeek article speculating that the Fed may hike short-term rates a quarter-point in early 1997, traders said. Eurodollar trade was brisk late. Talk of hedge funds selling in bonds.
Before traders could eye the next resistance level of 112-06/32 -- a level where sell-stop orders were hit on Thursday -- bonds backed down amid talk of hedge fund selling.
Talk that one prominent hedge fund manager was selling bonds sparked light selling in Eurodollars, one Eurodollar pit trader said.
Business was brisk in the Eurodollar pit late, while pit trade in bond futures languished late in the session.
The market's retreat from its highs was attributed in part to concerns about December's labor data next Friday and possible comments from Federal Reserve officials this weekend.
Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey, as well as other government officials, are scheduled to speak at the American Economic Association conference this weekend in New Orleans.

Many traders said a U.S. magazine article also pushed the market from its highs. The article in Business Week speculated that the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates a quarter point in early 1997.
While many traders cited the article for the market's reluctance to probe higher, they said the it provided little fresh information.
"It's really an excuse," one bond analyst said.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were up 06/32 at 111-18/32, 10-year notes were up 04/32 at 108-18/32, March Eurodollars were unchanged at 94.38, June Eurodollars were up one basis point at 94.20 and June T-bills were up two bps at 94.76.
